title: Mikhail Tal, the Magician from Riga
summary: Yugoslavia, 1959: the 22-year-old Tal sacrifices his queen against a former world champion, and wins the brilliancy prize.

steps.title: The magician from Riga
steps.text: Mikhail Tal played chess like a magician: pieces vanished from his board and reappeared in your nightmares. In 1959, at twenty-two, he faced Vasily Smyslov, a former world champion famous for impregnable defense, at the Candidates Tournament, with a world championship match at stake. Tal won this game with a queen sacrifice, took the brilliancy prize, and a year later was the youngest world champion in history. Press play.
steps.narration: Mikhail Tal, the magician from Riga. In 1959 he faced Smyslov, a former world champion, with a title match at stake. What he does in this game won the brilliancy prize. Press play.

steps.title: Tal – Smyslov, Candidates 1959
steps.text: Smyslov answers 1.e4 with the solid Caro-Kann. Tal responds the only way he knows: open lines, pieces forward, and a queen sacrifice that the chess world still talks about.
steps.narration: Smyslov chooses the solid Caro-Kann. Tal answers the only way he knows: open lines, pieces forward, and then the thunderbolt.

notes.text: 5.d4! Tal opens the center immediately: against Smyslov, quiet maneuvering would be playing his game.
9.O-O-O: Tal castles long. The kings glare at each other across an open board.
10.Nd6! The knight plants itself in Black's position, and it cannot be chased away.
13.Nf5! The knight eyes h6 and e7. The storm clouds gather over the black king.
14.Qh4! The queen slides to the kingside. Something is brewing: Smyslov can feel it.
15.Qg5! Every white piece is now aimed at the king. Black's knight jumps to h5 to block.
16.Nh6+! A shocking check: taking the knight would tear open the g-file.
17.Qxh5! Tal takes the knight. Smyslov grabs the a2 pawn with check, counterattacking…
19.Qxf7!! THE MOVE. Tal sacrifices his queen on the spot: the thunderbolt this game is famous for.
20.Kd2! The king calmly steps up. Black must take the queen, and walk into what Tal prepared.
21.Nxf7+! Check, and now Black's queen on a1 is lost. This was Tal's idea all along.
22.Rxa1: the queen is recaptured. When the smoke clears, Tal has won material with a crushing position.
26.Bd4! and Smyslov resigned. The judges gave Tal the tournament's brilliancy prize.

steps.title: Play the thunderbolt
steps.prompt: Black's knight just attacked your queen, and his queen is about to take on a2 with check. Every defender would save the queen. Tal did the opposite: find his move, then follow the combination.
steps.hint: The queen is not running away. She has one last job to do on f7.
steps.success: Qxf7!! Qa1+ Kd2! Rxf7 Nxf7+: the queen comes back with interest. You saw it the way Tal saw it.
steps.narration: Here is the moment. Your queen is attacked, and Tal's answer made this game immortal. Find it.

steps.title: The Tal style
steps.question: What made Mikhail Tal so terrifying to play against, even for world champions?

options.text: His sacrifices dragged opponents into complications only he could navigate
options.why: Exactly. Tal said there were two kinds of sacrifices: correct ones, and his. The complications did the rest.

options.text: He ground out tiny endgame edges for eighty moves
options.why: That was Smyslov's and Karpov's territory. Tal wanted the opposite: chaos, as early as possible.

options.text: He never took risks and waited for mistakes
options.why: Tal took risks almost every game: that was the whole point. His opponents' mistakes came from the pressure.

steps.narration: Last question: what exactly made Tal so terrifying?
